history.hpi: Patient was shot once in the left lower abdomen during an altercation outside a convenience store approximately 8 minutes prior to EMS arrival. Bystanders applied a t-shirt to the wound for direct pressure. Patient is diaphoretic, anxious, and reports severe abdominal pain with visible protruding bowel at the wound site.
history.lastOralIntake: Dinner approximately 3 hours prior to injury
history.events: Struck by a single gunshot during an altercation; bystanders called 911 immediately and applied direct pressure with a t-shirt

scene.dispatch: 31-year-old male, gunshot wound, altercation, police on scene
scene.location: Sidewalk outside a convenience store, urban area, nighttime
scene.safety: Scene secured by law enforcement prior to EMS entry; shooter fled and is not in custody
scene.bystanders: Several witnesses present; one applied direct pressure with a t-shirt prior to EMS arrival
visualCues: Single entry wound to left lower quadrant with a loop of bowel protruding through the wound
Moderate blood pooling on the ground and clothing
Patient supine, diaphoretic, clutching abdomen, guarding
No exit wound identified on initial visual sweep
Blood-soaked t-shirt applied by bystander over the wound

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 31-year-old male with a single gunshot wound to the left lower abdomen, with a loop of bowel eviscerated through the wound. Patient is alert, diaphoretic, tachycardic, and hypotensive with ongoing external hemorrhage partially controlled by a bystander dressing.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present but thready and rapid
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: Single GSW to left lower quadrant with visible bowel evisceration
Blood-soaked t-shirt over wound, ongoing oozing
Severe abdominal pain, 9/10, worse with movement
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It hurts so bad, please help me — I can see my insides."

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform MARCH primary survey; recognize penetrating torso trauma as high acuity
expectedActions.rationale: Structured primary survey ensures massive hemorrhage and airway threats are addressed before secondary exam.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reinforce direct pressure/wound packing at entry wound; roll and examine back for exit wound
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: First stop severe external and extremity hemorrhage with extremity tourniquets or appropriate wound packing with hemostatic gauze. Be sure to roll patient and examine the back as well.
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing external hemorrhage is a primary driver of this patient's shock and must be addressed immediately.

expectedActions.shortAction: Cover eviscerated bowel with moist sterile dressing; do not attempt to reduce contents
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Cover eviscerated abdominal contents with moist dressings
expectedActions.rationale: Attempting to push bowel back into the abdomen risks contamination and further injury; moist coverage protects exposed tissue.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish large-bore IV access en route without delaying transport
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access if needed (large bore preferred)
expectedActions.rationale: Vascular access supports fluid resuscitation but should not extend scene time for an unstable penetrating trauma patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Minimize scene time to under 10 minutes; initiate rapid transport to trauma center
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patients with major hemorrhage, hemodynamic instability, penetrating torso trauma, or signs of traumatic brain injury often require rapid surgical intervention. Minimize scene time (goal is under 10 minutes) and initiate rapid transport to the highest level of care within the trauma system
expectedActions.rationale: This patient has penetrating torso trauma with hemodynamic instability and needs surgical intervention rather than prolonged scene interventions.

transitions.condition: Crew performs a rapid MARCH primary survey, controls external hemorrhage, covers the evisceration with a moist sterile dressing, and prepares for rapid transport given penetrating torso trauma.
Instead of covering the eviscerated bowel in place, the crew attempts to manually push the protruding bowel back into the abdomen and applies a dry dressing, deviating from protocol.

phases.name: Primary survey and hemorrhage controlled
phases.description: Crew completes the MARCH primary survey, reinforces hemorrhage control at the wound site, covers the eviscerated bowel with a moist sterile dressing without attempting to reduce it, establishes IV access without delaying transport, and minimizes scene time given the penetrating torso trauma.
phases.triggerCondition: After a rapid MARCH primary survey, the crew identifies ongoing external hemorrhage from the entry wound and covers the eviscerated bowel with a moist sterile dressing rather than attempting to reduce it, while preparing for immediate transport given the penetrating torso trauma.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: Evisceration covered with moist sterile dressing, not reduced
Direct pressure reinforced over entry wound, oozing slowed
Large-bore IV established in right AC
No new deformities on secondary survey
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Okay... okay, just get me to the hospital."

expectedActions.shortAction: Give 500 mL crystalloid bolus targeting SBP 90 mmHg; reassess after bolus
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If SBP less than 90 mmHg or HR greater than 120 BPM, initiate resuscitation: ... consider 500 mL bolus of IV fluid, repeat as needed for persistent signs and symptoms of shock ... Trauma resuscitation target SBP 90 mmHg (palpable radial pulse or alert mental status). Reassess SBP after bolus given
expectedActions.rationale: Permissive hypotension avoids disrupting clot formation while maintaining adequate perfusion for an alert, penetrating-trauma patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide advance notification to trauma center using AT-MIST report
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use structured communication tool for patient handoff to higher level care such as AT-MIST
expectedActions.rationale: Advance notification allows the trauma team to mobilize surgical resources before arrival.

transitions.condition: En route, the crew targets a trauma resuscitation SBP of 90 mmHg rather than aggressively normalizing blood pressure, reassessing after each fluid bolus.

phases.name: Permissive hypotension maintained en route
phases.description: Crew titrates fluid boluses toward the trauma resuscitation target of SBP 90 mmHg rather than normalizing blood pressure, reassessing after each bolus, and provides advance notification to the receiving trauma center.
phases.triggerCondition: En route, the crew targets a trauma resuscitation SBP of 90 mmHg (palpable radial pulse or alert mental status) rather than aggressively normalizing blood pressure, reassessing after each fluid bolus to avoid disrupting early clot formation.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, palpable and steady
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: Dressing and packing intact, no new active bleeding
Advance notification given to trauma center with AT-MIST report
Mental status remains alert throughout transport
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Am I gonna be okay? Please don't let me die."

phases.name: Evisceration contents reduced improperly
phases.description: Crew mistakenly attempts to manually push the protruding bowel back into the abdominal cavity and applies a dry dressing instead of moist coverage, risking contamination and further tissue injury while delaying attention to ongoing hemorrhage.
phases.triggerCondition: Instead of covering the eviscerated bowel with a moist sterile dressing in place, the crew attempts to manually reduce the protruding bowel and applies a dry dressing, deviating from protocol and delaying reassessment of ongoing hemorrhage.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: Bowel manually reduced against protocol; dry dressing applied
Increased guarding and rigidity on reassessment

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize improper evisceration management; expose wound, apply moist sterile dressing, avoid reduction
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Cover eviscerated abdominal contents with moist dressings
expectedActions.rationale: Reducing eviscerated bowel and covering it with a dry dressing increases contamination and tissue injury risk; the crew must correct course immediately.
